mainTopic: Whether a woman married or betrothed to a כהן who is a פצוע דכא may eat תרומה: אביי and רבא's reasons, and רבי יוחנן's question about a בת גרים, settled by a ברייתא.
overview: The גמרא asks whether a woman betrothed to a כהן who is a פצוע דכא may eat תרומה. A proof from רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון is rejected, because a פצוע דכא may not marry a woman born Jewish, and whether he can feed a בת גרים was a question רבי יוחנן asked and never got answered. אביי and רבא each show a case where he does have power to feed: a wife he married before the injury, or his Canaanite slaves. Then each explains why he rejects the other's proof. The גמרא next tells the story of רבי יוחנן's question to רבי אושעיא, who stayed silent and said it had no solution. The question cannot fit רבי יהודה (she never eats) or רבי יוסי (she always eats), so it must follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: does a Jewish-born mother give her daughter only fitness, or full holiness? A ברייתא brought by רבי אחא בר חיננא shows that she gains only fitness, so she eats. The amud ends as a new dispute opens with רב.

steps.title: So this woman also eats
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof. Just as in the cases of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the woman betrothed to a פצוע דכא may also eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one may also eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up a proof it started just before this line. If רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון let other disqualified betrothed women eat תרומה, then a woman betrothed to a פצוע דכא may eat too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works by comparison. In the earlier cases, a woman who becomes forbidden to the כהן only through the completed marriage keeps eating until then. The same should apply to the פצוע דכא's betrothed.

keyTerms.meaning: This one too
She eats (תרומה)
A man with crushed testicles, forbidden to marry a woman born Jewish

phrases.english: this one may also eat.
phrases.notes: "This one" is the woman betrothed to a פצוע דכא. "Eat" means eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a proof begun before this section
steps.raayaObject: A woman betrothed to a פצוע דכא may eat תרומה until marriage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The view of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון in the משנה

steps.title: The comparison fails: he cannot feed anyone else
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון might only have been lenient when the כהן can feed a wife תרומה in another case. A פצוע דכא cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do you know? Maybe רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון only said it there, where he can feed a wife elsewhere. Here, where he cannot feed anyone elsewhere, they would not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. It points out a difference between the earlier cases and the פצוע דכא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases the כהן is a normal כהן who could marry another woman and feed her תרומה. A פצוע דכא is not allowed to marry a woman born Jewish, so he has no power to feed anyone. That difference may matter.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know?
Perhaps
They only said it in this case
To feed (to entitle someone to eat תרומה)
In another case

steps.confusionAlert: "Feeding" here does not mean giving food. It means the כהן's status gives a woman the right to eat תרומה.

phrases.english: From where do you know this?
Perhaps they only said it
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon, there,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא דְּיֵשׁ לוֹ לְהַאֲכִיל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר.
phrases.english: where he can entitle a woman to eat in another case.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, דְּאֵין לוֹ לְהַאֲכִיל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר — לָא.
phrases.english: But here, where he cannot entitle anyone in another case, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 1
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the משנה's cases and the פצוע דכא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A normal כהן can feed a wife elsewhere, but a פצוע דכא cannot

steps.title: Marrying a convert's daughter does not help
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say a פצוע דכא can feed a בת גרים whom he marries. But רבי יוחנן asked רבי אושעיא about that very case, and it was never resolved.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say that here too he can feed a convert's daughter, wasn't this asked by רבי יוחנן of רבי אושעיא, and he did not resolve it for him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks a possible comeback to its rejection, which makes the rejection stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פצוע דכא may marry a בת גרים, so maybe he can feed her תרומה. But רבי יוחנן asked רבי אושעיא this exact question, and רבי אושעיא did not resolve it. So at this point we cannot say for sure that he has power to feed anyone. Step 24 later settles this question.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say
Daughter of converts
He raised it as a question
And he did not resolve it for him

phrases.english: And if you say: here too
he can entitle a convert's daughter to eat,
wasn't it raised as a question
by Rabbi Yochanan to Rabbi Oshaya,
and he did not resolve it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers a possible defense of the proof, so the rejection in step 2 still stands
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that a בת גרים gives the פצוע דכא power to feed
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Whether a בת גרים eats in this case was never resolved
steps.whatToRemember: The proof is rejected. A פצוע דכא seems to have no clear power to feed any woman תרומה, so he may differ from the cases of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.

steps.title: אביי: he can feed a wife he has not yet been with
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the פצוע דכא does have power to feed. If a כהן married properly and then became a פצוע דכא, his wife keeps eating until they are together.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: אביי said: since he can feed her when he has not been with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings אביי, who shows that a פצוע דכא can feed a wife תרומה in another case. That brings back the comparison to רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 claimed he cannot feed anyone. אביי answers with a case: a כהן already married who was later injured. His wife eats as long as he has not been with her since the injury, so he does have power to feed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces an אמוראים teaching)
Since
He entitles her to eat
When he has not been intimate with her

phrases.english: It was stated: Abaye said:
Since he can entitle her to eat when he has not been with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in steps 2-3 by finding a case where he can feed
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies another case where he has power to feed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פצוע דכא has no power to feed anyone
steps.terutzMaskana: He can feed a wife he married before the injury, until he is with her

steps.title: רבא: he can feed his Canaanite slaves
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives another reason: the פצוע דכא can feed his Canaanite slaves and maidservants תרומה, so he does have power to feed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: since he can feed his Canaanite slaves and maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different answer from אביי for why the פצוע דכא has power to feed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא points to a simpler case. A כהן's Canaanite slaves eat תרומה, and this is true of a פצוע דכא too. Since he has this power, his case matches the cases of רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, and his betrothed may eat.

keyTerms.meaning: His male and female slaves
Canaanite (non-Jewish slaves owned by a Jew)

steps.whatToRemember: Both אביי and רבא agree that the woman betrothed to a פצוע דכא eats תרומה, because he does have power to feed. They differ only on which case shows that power: a wife he has not been with (אביי) or his Canaanite slaves (רבא).

phrases.english: Rava said:
Since he entitles his Canaanite slaves and maidservants to eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reason from אביי's to answer the same rejection
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a different case where he has power to feed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A פצוע דכא has no power to feed anyone
steps.terutzMaskana: He feeds his Canaanite slaves, so the comparison holds

steps.title: Why אביי does not accept רבא's proof from slaves
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבא's proof because you cannot learn the rules of marriage from the rules of owning slaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי did not agree with רבא's reason. We learn the rules of a marriage from another marriage. We do not learn the rules of a marriage from the rules of owning slaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why אביי did not use רבא's proof about slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא showed that a פצוע דכא can feed his slaves תרומה, so he has the power to feed. אביי says that proves nothing about a wife, because owning a slave and being married are two different kinds of קנין. Only a marriage case, like his own, can teach about marriage.

keyTerms.meaning: the bond of marriage, the husband's 'ownership' connection to his wife
the ownership a master has over his slaves
we learn or derive (one law from another)

phrases.english: Abaye did not say like Rava,
because we learn the bond of marriage from the bond of marriage,
and we do not learn the bond of marriage
from the ownership of slaves.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבא's proof in step 5, that a פצוע דכא feeds his slaves תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why אביי does not accept רבא's answer from step 5.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A slave-ownership case cannot teach a law about marriage; they are different kinds of קנין.

steps.title: Why רבא does not accept אביי's proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects אביי's proof because in אביי's case the wife had already been eating תרומה before he was injured.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא did not agree with אביי's reason. That case is different, because she had already been eating תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains why רבא did not use אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's case was a כהן who married properly and only later became a פצוע דכא. רבא says the wife there keeps eating only because she already started eating while he was healthy. That does not show that a פצוע דכא can give a new wife the right to eat.

keyTerms.meaning: it is different there (that case is not the same)
because she had already eaten (תרומה)

phrases.english: And Rava did not say like Abaye,
because it is different there, since she had already eaten.
phrases.notes: "There" is אביי's case from step 4, where the כהן became injured only after the marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The other side of the pair: after explaining אביי's objection to רבא, the גמרא explains רבא's objection to אביי.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: אביי's proof from a כהן who became a פצוע דכא after marriage
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that case she keeps eating only because she already started eating, so it says nothing about a fresh marriage.

steps.title: אביי's challenge: then a priest's widow should also eat
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that 'she already ate' cannot be a reason, because then a בת ישראל whose כהן husband died should keep eating too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: we do not say 'she already ate.' If you did, then a בת ישראל who married a כהן and he died should keep eating תרומה, since she already ate.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי fights back against רבא's reason by showing it leads to a result everyone knows is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that a בת ישראל whose כהן husband died stops eating תרומה. But she also 'already ate' while he was alive. So, says אביי, having already eaten cannot be what lets a woman keep eating.

keyTerms.meaning: for if you do not say so (if you held the opposite)
a daughter of a regular Jew, not of a כהן
she should eat

phrases.english: And Abaye: we do not say 'since she already ate,'
for if you do not say so,
a daughter of an Israelite who married a priest and he died
should eat, since she already ate.
phrases.notes: This is said as something obviously wrong: everyone knows she may not eat after he dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבא's distinction from step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If already eating let a woman continue, a כהן's widow would continue too, which is clearly false.

steps.title: רבא answers: death ends the marriage, injury does not
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that when the כהן dies his bond with her ends, but when he becomes a פצוע דכא she is still his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא answers: there, his bond with her ended. Here, his bond with her did not end.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his reason by showing why the widow's case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having already eaten only helps if the marriage still exists. When the כהן dies, the marriage is over, so there is nothing left to keep her eating. When he becomes a פצוע דכא, she is still his wife, so her earlier right to eat continues.

keyTerms.meaning: his bond (ownership) ended, fell away
here (in our case)

steps.whatToRemember: אביי learns marriage only from marriage. רבא says the injured husband's wife keeps eating only because she already ate and the marriage never ended.

phrases.english: And Rava: there, his bond ended,
here, his bond did not end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Already eating should let any woman continue, even a widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: Already eating only helps while the marriage is still alive; death ends it, injury does not.

steps.title: The story of רבי יוחנן's unanswered question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the question רבי יוחנן asked רבי אושעיא. רבי אושעיא stayed silent, but later answered a different question from ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now to the question itself. רבי יוחנן asked רבי אושעיא: a כהן who is a פצוע דכא and married a בת גרים, may he feed her תרומה? He was silent and said nothing at all. Later another great man came, asked him a different question, and he answered it. Who was he? ריש לקיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question mentioned earlier in step 3 and tells the full story behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא only mentioned that רבי אושעיא did not answer this question. Now it tells what happened: רבי אושעיא did not answer רבי יוחנן, yet he did answer ריש לקיש. This sets up the next step, where someone asks why he treated them differently.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': the גמרא now discusses in full something it mentioned in passing
the daughter of converts
he was silent
he answered (resolved) it for him

phrases.aramaic: גּוּפָא, בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Yochanan asked Rabbi Oshaya:
phrases.notes: This is the question mentioned back in step 3.

phrases.aramaic: פְּצוּעַ דַּכָּא כֹּהֵן שֶׁנָּשָׂא בַּת גֵּרִים.
phrases.english: A priest with crushed organs who married the daughter of converts,
may he feed her teruma?

phrases.aramaic: אִישְׁתִּיק וְלָא אֲמַר לֵיהּ וְלָא מִידֵּי.
phrases.english: He was silent and said nothing to him at all.
In the end another great man came
and asked him a different matter, and he answered it for him.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets, "different," is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: And who was he? Reish Lakish.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אביי-רבא discussion and returns to the question mentioned in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן's question about a פצוע דכא כהן married to a בת גרים was met with silence.

steps.title: רבי יהודה נשיאה asks why רבי יוחנן got no answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה נשיאה asks רבי אושעיא: isn't רבי יוחנן also a great man? Why didn't you answer him?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה נשיאה said to רבי אושעיא: Is רבי יוחנן not a great man?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה נשיאה questions why רבי אושעיא answered ריש לקיש but ignored רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question suggests רבי אושעיא was being disrespectful, as if he thought רבי יוחנן was less important. This sets up רבי אושעיא's explanation in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: 'is it so that...?', introducing a surprised question
a great man, a great scholar

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה לְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda Nesia said to Rabbi Oshaya:

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָאו גַּבְרָא רַבָּה הוּא?
phrases.english: Is Rabbi Yochanan not a great man?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה נְשִׂיאָה לְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to the story in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אושעיא did not answer רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: the question has no answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא explains that he was silent because רבי יוחנן's question has no solution.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: because he asked me something that has no solution.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אושעיא explains his silence: it was not disrespect, he simply had no solution to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The silence was not about who asked. רבי אושעיא held that he had no answer to give. The גמרא will now work out which view the question fits, and in steps 22-24 it finds a ברייתא that answers it after all.

keyTerms.meaning: that has no solution

phrases.english: He said to him: because he asked me a matter
that has no solution.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהודה נשיאה's question from step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אושעיא had no solution to the question, so he had nothing to answer. The גמרא later answers it in step 24.

steps.title: According to whose view was the question asked?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא's view רבי יוחנן's question was based on, to see where the question really fits.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up its explanation of why the question has no solution by asking which opinion it follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether a בת גרים may marry a כהן is a dispute among תנאים. The גמרא will show that under רבי יהודה and under רבי יוסי the answer is already clear. Then it finds the one view, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, where the question is real.

keyTerms.meaning: according to whom?

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to explain רבי אושעיא's claim in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which opinion about a בת גרים marrying a כהן the question is based on.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה, she cannot eat either way
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי יהודה, whether the פצוע דכא still has the holiness of a כהן or not, she may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is according to רבי יהודה: whether he still has his holiness as a כהן or does not, she does not eat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks the first option, רבי יהודה's view, and says both sides lead to the same answer: she may not eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways to see a פצוע דכא: he either keeps the holiness of a כהן or he loses it. Under רבי יהודה, both ways end with her not eating תרומה, so there is nothing to ask. The גמרא will now explain each side.

keyTerms.meaning: he stays in his holiness (still counts as a full כהן)
whether... or...

phrases.english: If according to Rabbi Yehuda,
whether he remains in his holiness
or he does not remain in his holiness,
she does not eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to 'according to whom?' from step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under רבי יהודה, she does not eat in either case.

steps.title: If he is still a full priest, a convert's daughter is like a חלל's daughter
steps.stepSummary: If the פצוע דכא still has the holiness of a כהן, she cannot eat, because רבי יהודה holds that a male convert's daughter is like a male חלל's daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he still has his holiness, she does not eat, for the Master said: the daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male חלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first side of רבי יהודה's 'either way' and backs it up with a known rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חלל's daughter may not marry a כהן, so she cannot eat תרומה through him. רבי יהודה treats a convert's daughter the same way. So if the פצוע דכא is still a full כהן, this marriage is forbidden to him and she cannot eat.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the Master said', quoting a known teaching
the daughter of a male convert
a son of a כהן from a marriage forbidden to a כהן; he loses כהונה status

steps.confusionAlert: This only explains the first side, where he is still a full כהן. The other side, where he lost that holiness, still has to be explained.

phrases.english: If he remains in his holiness, she does not eat,
for the Master said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת גֵּר זָכָר כְּבַת חָלָל זָכָר.
phrases.english: The daughter of a male convert is like the daughter of a male chalal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי בִּקְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ קָאֵי — לָא אָכְלָה, דְּהָא אָמַר מָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first side of the 'either way' in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That under רבי יהודה, if the פצוע דכא keeps his holiness, a בת גרים cannot eat תרומה through him
steps.raayaSupportSource: The known teaching: a male convert's daughter is like a male חלל's daughter.

steps.title: According to רבי יהודה, she also cannot eat if he lost his holiness
steps.stepSummary: Even if the פצוע דכא no longer has the holiness of a כהן, she still cannot eat תרומה. This is because רבי יהודה holds that a congregation of converts counts as a 'קהל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he no longer has his holiness, she still does not eat. We say that according to רבי יהודה, a congregation of converts is called 'קהל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second side of רבי יהודה's view. Even if the injured כהן lost his special status, his wife still cannot eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פצוע דכא is now treated like a regular person with this injury, the rule against him entering the קהל applies. Since רבי יהודה counts converts as part of the קהל, his marriage to a daughter of converts is forbidden. So she cannot eat. Both sides lead to 'no', so according to רבי יהודה there is no question at all.

keyTerms.meaning: The congregation of converts
Is called 'קהל', meaning the congregation a פצוע דכא may not marry into
He does not remain in his (priestly) holiness

phrases.english: If he does not remain in his holiness —
she does not eat,
for we say:
the congregation of converts is called 'congregation'.
phrases.notes: The פסוק that keeps a פצוע דכא out of the 'קהל' is דברים 23:2. So if converts count as קהל, he can't marry them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו בִּקְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ קָאֵי — לָא אָכְלָה, דְּהָא אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the proof from step 15. Step 15 covered the case where he keeps his holiness; this step covers the case where he does not.
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי יהודה she cannot eat even if the פצוע דכא lost his priestly holiness
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהודה's position that קהל גרים is called קהל

steps.title: According to רבי יוסי, she eats either way
steps.stepSummary: If the question were asked according to רבי יוסי, the answer would be 'she eats' on both sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it were according to רבי יוסי: whether he keeps his holiness or does not, she eats.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now checks the other תנא, רבי יוסי. It states the bottom line first: according to him, she eats no matter what. The next two steps will explain why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With רבי יהודה both sides gave 'no'. With רבי יוסי both sides give 'yes'. Either way, the doubt about his holiness makes no difference, so there is nothing to ask.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who argues with רבי יהודה about converts
Whether... or... (both cases)
She eats (תרומה)

phrases.english: And if according to Rabbi Yosei,
whether he remains in his holiness
or he does not remain in his holiness —
she eats.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי, בֵּין בִּקְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ קָאֵי בֵּין לָאו בִּקְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ קָאֵי — אָכְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 14. After showing that רבי יהודה's view leaves no question, the גמרא tests רבי יוסי's view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view could רבי יוחנן's question be based on?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not רבי יוסי, because according to him she always eats.

steps.title: If he keeps his holiness, she eats, because a convert's daughter can marry a כהן
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that even the daughter of two converts may marry a כהן. So if the פצוע דכא is still a כהן, she eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he keeps his holiness, she eats. רבי יוסי said: even a convert who married a female convert, his daughter is fit for כהונה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the first side of רבי יוסי's view: the case where the injured man is still treated as a full כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is still a כהן, the only question is whether a בת גרים may marry a כהן. רבי יוסי allows it even when both parents are converts. So the marriage is fine and she eats תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: A male convert who married a female convert
Fit to marry a כהן

phrases.english: If he remains in his holiness — she eats,
for he said:
even a convert who married a female convert —
his daughter is fit for the priesthood.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּקְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ קָאֵי — אָכְלָה, דְּהָא אָמַר: אַף גֵּר שֶׁנָּשָׂא גִּיּוֹרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the first half of step 17's claim.
steps.raayaObject: According to רבי יוסי she eats if the פצוע דכא keeps his priestly holiness
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי: even a convert who married a convert, his daughter is fit for כהונה

steps.title: If he lost his holiness, she eats, because converts are not called קהל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי holds that converts are not part of the 'קהל'. So even a regular פצוע דכא may marry a daughter of converts, and she eats.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he does not keep his holiness, she eats. רבי יוסי said: the congregation of converts is not called 'קהל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the second side of רבי יוסי's view. This finishes showing that his view leaves no question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he is treated like a regular פצוע דכא, the only problem would be the rule against entering the קהל. רבי יוסי says converts are not part of the קהל, so this marriage is allowed. Both sides give 'yes', the opposite of רבי יהודה, where both sides gave 'no'.

keyTerms.meaning: Is not called 'קהל'

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: she never eats. רבי יוסי: she always eats. According to either of them, the question about his holiness changes nothing.

phrases.english: If he does not remain in his holiness — she eats,
for he said:
the congregation of converts is not called 'congregation'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי לָאו בִּקְדוּשְׁתֵּיהּ קָאֵי — אָכְלָה, דְּהָא אָמַר: קְהַל גֵּרִים לָא אִיקְּרִי קָהָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of step 17's claim and closes the check of רבי יוסי's view.
steps.raayaObject: According to רבי יוסי she eats even if the פצוע דכא lost his priestly holiness
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוסי: קהל גרים is not called קהל

steps.title: The question follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's question must be based on רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. He says a daughter of converts may marry a כהן only if her mother was born Jewish.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the question follows this תנא, as we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, a woman who is a daughter of converts may not marry into כהונה unless her mother is from ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the question makes no sense according to רבי יהודה or רבי יוסי, the גמרא finds the תנא it does fit: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. This answers the question from step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב takes a middle view. A daughter of two converts may not marry a כהן. But if only the father is a convert and the mother is born Jewish, she may. So the case of רבי יוחנן's question must be a woman like this.

keyTerms.meaning: According to this תנא
The תנא with the middle view on converts' daughters
A daughter of converts
Her mother is born Jewish

phrases.english: Rather, it is according to this Tanna:
as we learned in a Mishnah,
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
a woman who is a daughter of converts
may not marry into the priesthood
unless her mother is from Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַלִּיבָּא דְּהַאי תַּנָּא: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ruling out רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי, the גמרא gives the real answer to step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view was רבי יוחנן's question based on?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who allows a convert's daughter to marry a כהן only if her mother is born Jewish.

steps.title: The real question: did she gain fitness or holiness?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was asking what a Jewish-born mother gives her daughter. Is it only fitness to marry a כהן, so she eats? Or is it holiness that makes her part of the קהל, so she does not eat?
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what he was asking: is fitness added to her, so she eats? Or perhaps holiness is added to her, so she does not eat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now states exactly what רבי יוחנן's question was according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. This shows why it is a real doubt that רבי אושעיא could not answer. The next step brings a source to settle it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Option one: the Jewish mother only makes the daughter 'fit' to marry a כהן. She is still not part of the קהל, so a פצוע דכא may marry her, and she eats. Option two: the Jewish mother gives her 'holiness', making her part of the קהל. Then the פצוע דכא may not marry her, and she does not eat.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what he was asking
Fitness (to marry a כהן)
Holiness (being part of the קהל)
Is added to her

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's question only works according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. The doubt is whether the Jewish mother gives the daughter only כשרות (she eats) or full קדושה (she does not eat). רבי אושעיא had no answer for it, but the ברייתא in steps 22-24 settles it.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Fitness' here does not mean she is less acceptable. It means she is allowed to marry a כהן without becoming part of the קהל. Ironically, that is exactly what would let her marry a פצוע דכא and eat.

phrases.english: And this is what he was asking:
is it fitness that is added to her —
and so she eats,
or perhaps it is holiness that is added to her —
and so she does not eat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ: כַּשְׁרוּת מִיתּוֹסְפָא בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the Tanna named in step 20 to spell out רבי יוחנן's exact question and show why it has no solution, as רבי אושעיא said in step 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the question is whether a Jewish-born mother gives her daughter only כשרות or full קדושה. רבי אושעיא had no answer, which explains his silence. Step 24 settles it.

steps.title: A ברייתא from the south about a פצוע דכא and a daughter of converts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from רבי אחא בר חיננא. It says a כהן who is a פצוע דכא, and who married a daughter of converts, may feed her תרומה. The source is the פסוק about a כהן's acquisition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When רבי אחא בר חיננא came from the south, he brought a ברייתא with him. It says: How do we know that a כהן who is a פצוע דכא and married a daughter of converts may feed her תרומה? Because the פסוק says, 'But if a כהן buys a soul, the purchase of his money... he may eat of it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to try to answer רבי יוחנן's question. The source is a ברייתא that says this wife eats תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא rules that a daughter of converts married to a פצוע דכא כהן eats תרומה. The פסוק says that whatever a כהן acquires may eat, and his wife counts as his acquisition. The next steps will work out which תנא this ברייתא follows, and that will show what it proves.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא is bringing a source to answer a question
A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
From the south
The purchase of his money. Here it includes a כהן's wife

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֲתָא רַבִּי אַחָא בַּר חִינָּנָא מִדָּרוֹמָא,
phrases.english: When Rabbi Acha bar Chinnana came from the south,
he came and brought a baraita in his hand:
From where do we know that a priest with crushed testicles
who married a daughter of converts
may feed her teruma?
As it is said:
"But if a priest buys a soul,
the purchase of his money, etc., he may eat of it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to answer the question stated in step 21.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a Jewish-born mother gives her daughter only fitness (so she eats) or holiness of the קהל (so she does not eat).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אחא בר חיננא, based on ויקרא 22:11.

steps.title: Whose view is this ברייתא? Not רבי יהודה and not רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא follows. It rules out רבי יהודה, because he says she never eats. It rules out רבי יוסי, because he says she always eats, so no פסוק would be needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say רבי יהודה: he said that whether the פצוע דכא still has his holiness as a כהן or not, she does not eat. And if you say רבי יוסי: why would we need a פסוק? He said that whether he still has his holiness or not, she eats!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks which תנא could have taught this ברייתא. It crosses off two options.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the ברייתא contradicts his view, because he says this wife cannot eat either way. For רבי יוסי, the ruling is already obvious, so a special פסוק would be pointless. Crossing off these two sets up the next step, which says the ברייתא must follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Which תנא holds this view?
If you say (the first option being tested)
He stays in his holiness, meaning he is still treated as a כהן
Why do I need a פסוק? The point is already known without one

steps.confusionAlert: The two "either way" lines sound alike, but they end opposite ways. For רבי יהודה it is "she does not eat." For רבי יוסי it is "she eats." Each one rules out that תנא for a different reason.

phrases.english: According to whom?
If we say according to Rabbi Yehuda,
didn't he say:
whether he remains in his sanctity
or whether he does not remain in his sanctity
she does not eat.
And if according to Rabbi Yosei,
why do I need a verse?
Didn't he say:
whether he remains in his sanctity
or whether he does not remain in his sanctity
she eats!
phrases.notes: This is the rule from step 19, so for רבי יוסי the פסוק would teach nothing new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out which תנא the ברייתא of step 22 follows, using the views laid out in steps 17 to 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view the ברייתא follows.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the mother adds only fitness
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא cannot follow רבי יהודה or רבי יוסי, it must follow רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. That proves the Jewish-born mother adds only fitness (כשרות), so the daughter eats תרומה. The גמרא accepts this proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it must be רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Learn from this that fitness was added to her, and she eats. Yes, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. This answers רבי יוחנן's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the daughter of converts in this ברייתא must have a Jewish-born mother. The ברייתא says she may eat even when married to a פצוע דכא. So her mother made her fit to marry a כהן, but did not make her part of the קהל, because then she would be forbidden to him. "שמע מינה" at the end means the proof stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not...? It points to the only option left
Learn from it. Said again at the end, it means the proof is accepted
Fitness, here meaning fit to marry a כהן
Was added

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, a Jewish-born mother gives her daughter only כשרות (fitness for כהונה), not the status of the קהל. So a daughter of converts with a Jewish-born mother, married to a כהן who is a פצוע דכא, eats תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This settles רבי יוחנן's question from step 21. The extra that a Jewish-born mother gives is fitness only, not holiness.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לָאו, לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: Rather, is it not according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?
And learn from it
that fitness was added to her
and she eats.
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו, לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Once two options are ruled out in step 23, this step names the only one left and draws the proof from it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A Jewish-born mother adds only fitness (כשרות) to her daughter, so the daughter eats תרומה even when married to a פצוע דכא.

steps.title: A new dispute begins with רב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new מחלוקת between אמוראים with the words "It was stated: רב said." רב's actual statement comes next.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It starts a new מחלוקת between אמוראים, and רב's words come right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "איתמר" tells us a new disagreement between אמוראים is starting, on a topic connected to what came before. Here we only have the opening and who speaks first. The ruling itself follows.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. It opens a disagreement between אמוראים
רב, a leading early אמורא of Babylonia

phrases.english: It was stated:
Rav said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the question is settled, the גמרא moves on to a new, related מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב's ruling comes right after this opening line.
